title: 2010 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: For what value of \(x\) does \[ \begin{aligned} &\log_{\sqrt2}\sqrt{x}+\log_2 x \\ &\quad {}+\log_4\left(x^2\right)+\log_8\left(x^3\right) \\ &\quad {}+\log_{16}\left(x^4\right)=40? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text:
Let \(L=\log_2 x.\) Converting each term to base \(2:\)

\(\log_{\sqrt2}\sqrt{x}=\dfrac{\frac{L}{2}}{\frac{1}{2}}=L,\) \(\log_2 x=L,\) \(\log_4 x^2=\dfrac{2L}{2}=L,\) \(\log_8 x^3=\dfrac{3L}{3}=L,\) and \(\log_{16}x^4=\dfrac{4L}{4}=L.\)

The equation becomes \(5L=40,\) so \(L=8\) and \(x=2^8=256.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Convert every term to base \(2;\) let \(L=\log_2 x\)
